subtype: Missing hunger or the need for the toilet [Actor]
passage:
Last Sunday, my cousin Lavanya and I built a huge castle with building blocks. We didn't stop for lunch. I didn't even notice I was hungry or that I needed the toilet.
Then one tower fell over, and I just burst. I threw a block and yelled at Lavanya, even though it wasn't her fault.
Mummy came in and asked, "When did you last eat? Or go to the toilet?" I realised I was starving and really needed to go. After a sandwich and water I felt normal again, and said sorry to Lavanya.
Now we have a rule. When the kitchen timer rings, we do a body check: tummy, water, toilet. It's a bit annoying. But the castle hasn't been attacked since.

Shreya

qa.a: Lavanya was probably hurt and confused, since the tower falling wasn't her fault.

grounding: It shows a child absorbed in play ignoring hunger and the need for the toilet, falling apart, and learning a quick body check.

passage:
Art camp note, Thursday

Ujjwal, age eight, was so absorbed in his painting this morning that he didn't go to the toilet or touch his snack. Just before lunch he suddenly jumped up, holding himself, and burst into tears. He made it to the toilet just in time, but was very upset and embarrassed.
I helped him quietly, without any fuss, and told him it happens to lots of people when they are focused.
This afternoon we started a "body check" for the whole class at every bell: am I hungry, thirsty, need the toilet? Ujjwal liked calling it out. At the last bell he went to the toilet by himself before starting a new painting.
I will tell his parents so they can try it at home.

Mahima

qa.q: What did Ujjwal forget to touch while painting?
How did Ujjwal feel just before lunch?
qa.a: He felt upset and embarrassed after suddenly realising how badly he needed the toilet.

qa.q: What did Mahima set up, and why does it help?
qa.a: A class body check at every bell, which helps children like Ujjwal notice hunger, thirst and the toilet before it becomes urgent.

qa.q: How might Ujjwal's parents feel reading this note?
qa.a: They would likely be grateful he was helped quietly and pleased to have a simple habit to try at home.

grounding: It shows a child absorbed in painting who ignores his body until it becomes urgent, and a quick body check building awareness over time.
